key_insight: LUCQUE introduces a large, comprehensively annotated lung cancer screening dataset from Québec. It is designed to support more reproducible, comparable, and independent evaluation of AI screening tools.
problem_solved: AI evaluation in lung cancer screening has relied on private or fragmented public datasets with inconsistent clinical information and expert nodule annotations, making results difficult to reproduce and compare.
method: Build a dataset from low-dose CT (LDCT) lung cancer screening in Québec.
Provide comprehensive annotations to address gaps in existing evaluation datasets.
Establish a shared resource for assessing AI screening tools; dataset size and annotation protocols are not specified in the provided abstract excerpt.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, LUCQUE could provide a stronger foundation for benchmarking and independently assessing lung cancer screening models. The supplied excerpt does not report quantitative evaluation results.
visual_elements: Dataset pipeline: Québec screening program → LDCT scans → annotations → AI evaluation.
Lung CT illustration with a highlighted nodule to explain the screening task.
Side-by-side schematic contrasting fragmented evaluation resources with a comprehensively annotated dataset.
Three icons representing reproducibility, comparability, and independent assessment.
paper_title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Québec for reliable AI evaluation
paper_authors: Johanna Topalis, Yannick Lemaréchal, Gabriel Couture, Hanife Ersay, Loran Nas
